Full suite green: 1628 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Lint clean.

**Root cause.** The remotes list was derived from *refs*, not from *config*. `jjRemoteState` built it from `jj bookmark list --all-remotes` — but `jj git remote add` creates no remote bookmarks, so your repo listed only `master` and `@git`, `remotes` came back empty, `primaryRemote` was nil, and the header hit tier [3] "No remote configured". Verified on `workroom-play-jj`: `jj git remote list` shows origin, `jj bookmark list --all-remotes` shows no `@origin` row.

Git had the identical latent bug (`git remote add` writes config, no `refs/remotes/*`), so both paths are fixed.

**Changes** — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift`:
- `jjRemoteListArgs()` / `gitRemoteListArgs()` — read configured remotes (`jj git remote list`, `git remote`). `--ignore-working-copy` is mandatory on the jj one: without it that command takes the **Git import/export lock**, which no other read here does.
- `parseJJRemoteList` / `parseGitRemoteList` — jj splits on the *last* space (names may contain spaces, URLs don't); drops the `git` pseudo-remote.
- `mergeRemotes(configured:derived:)` — union, config order first, so a failed remote-list call degrades to the old ref-derived answer instead of blanking a working toolbar.

Second defect in the same family, fixed for git parity: a jj bookmark with no `@origin` row left `tracking` nil, which fell through to the fetch tier — the toolbar offered "Never fetched"/Fetch, and fetching can never create the counterpart, so a freshly-remoted repo was permanently stuck. Now reported `gone: true`, so you get **Publish branch** like git.

Tests: 2 integration tests (jj + git, remote added and never fetched), 5 parser/merge unit tests.

Your `workroom-play-jj` should now read "Publish branch — master isn't on origin yet".

140	  private func load() {
141	    guard let target else { return }
142	    task?.cancel()
143	    state = .loading
144	    let makeWriter = self.makeWriter

146	    task = Task { [weak self] in
147	      if debounce > 0 {

150	      }

152	      let resolution: VCSRemoteResolution
153	      do {
154	        resolution = await (try makeWriter(root)).remoteState(
155	          path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot)

164	  private func apply(_ resolution: VCSRemoteResolution, for target: Target) {
165	    // A read that finished after the model moved on must not overwrite the new target's state.
166	    guard self.target == target else { return }
167	    switch resolution {
168	    case .state(let state):
169	      // Merge in Workroom's own fetch record. Needed because jj's fetch is invisible: it passes
170	      // `--no-write-fetch-head`, and a fetch that brings nothing records NO operation at all — so the
171	      // op-log scan alone would mean "last fetch that changed something", and clicking Fetch with
172	      // nothing new would leave a stale timestamp on screen. The backend still wins when it is newer,
173	      // which keeps a fetch run in the user's own terminal visible.
174	      snapshot = Self.merging(state, ownFetch: Defaults[.vcsLastFetch][target.projectRoot])
175	      self.state = .loaded
176	      onBranchResolved?(target.sid, state.current.name)
177	    case .absent:
178	      snapshot = nil
179	      self.state = .loaded
180	      onBranchResolved?(target.sid, nil)
181	    case .keepPrior:
182	      // A transient blip — leave the last good snapshot standing rather than blanking the toolbar.
183	      self.state = snapshot == nil ? .idle : .loaded
184	    case .failed(let failure):
185	      snapshot = nil
186	      self.state = .failed(VCSSyncPresenter.describe(failure))
187	      onBranchResolved?(target.sid, nil)
188	    }
189	  }

Done. Dialog now carries the failure; bar keeps the one-line notice.

**What happens now.** A user-initiated fetch/push/pull that fails raises a sheet: warning glyph, "Push failed", the full message (never truncated, selectable), a collapsed **Details** disclosure holding the tool's raw stderr in a scrollable monospaced box, and the actions — `Copy`, `Reveal in Finder` (located lock only), `Dismiss` (Esc), and the recovery as the default button (Return). Your case reads:

> Describe the change before pushing it (jj describe).
>
> Give the change a message first, then push again:
>
> jj describe -m "…"

**Design decisions worth knowing:**
- **Auto-fetch stays silent.** It's a network call nobody asked for, so a failure there records `lastFailure` for the toolbar and raises no dialog — `perform(_:userInitiated:)`, `false` only from `autoFetchIfDue`.
- **The bar's behaviour is unchanged.** Same tier, same one-click recovery, same disabled-with-no-recovery rule. Dismissing the dialog doesn't clear `lastFailure` — the failure hasn't stopped being true. Right-click the segment → **Show Error Details…** re-opens it.
- **No doomed default button.** The dialog's primary comes from the same `retryAction` the bar uses, so `needsDescription` / `immutableHistory` / located-lock get no Return-key retry.
- **Hosted on RootView, not the inspector** — ⌥⇧⌘P works with the inspector hidden, and a dialog that only appears when a pane happens to be open is worse than none.
- Recovery routes through `store.performRemoteAction`, so a Pull recovery still meets the dirty-tree autostash confirmation.

Per-failure remedies written for all 11 cases (auth, host key, no remote, rejected, dirty tree, rebase in progress, immutable history, needs description, tool missing, timeout; located lock keeps its existing full explanation).

One gotcha found by the UI test: an `.accessibilityIdentifier` on the sheet's container made SwiftUI absorb every child element — sheet findable, title/message/buttons not. Fixed with `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)`, and it's commented as such.

Tests: 6 model tests, 5 presenter tests, 2 XCUITests (both backends). Full unit suite 1641 passed / 0 failed, toolbar UI suite 20 passed, lint clean. Not committed.

message, the tool's own output under a Details disclosure, and every action
there is — Copy, Reveal in Finder for a located lock, Dismiss, and the
recovery as the default button. Each failure gains a written remedy; the
located lock keeps the full explanation it already had.

The toolbar tier is unchanged: same copy, same one-click recovery, same
refusal to offer a retry that would fail identically — the dialog's default
button comes from the same `retryAction`, so the two can't disagree. Dismissing
leaves `lastFailure` standing, since the failure hasn't stopped being true, and
the segment's context menu reopens the dialog.

nobody asked for, so failing it must be as quiet as succeeding it. Hosted on
RootView rather than the inspector, because ⌥⇧⌘P works with the inspector
hidden and a dialog that needs a particular pane open is worse than none.

`children: .contain` on the sheet is load-bearing: an accessibility identifier
